The source evidence storage contract operates as a temporal-spatial filter over roster facts, where each entry is timestamped and hashed to ensure integrity. The reconciliation process applies a precedence rule: official records override fallbacks, and newer transactions supersede older ones. This creates a dual-layered validation system—first, evidence is stored with metadata; second, it is validated against known truths. Failure modes include stale data rendering, unresolvable conflicts, and missing source links. These are mitigated through rollback plans and telemetry-driven alerts. The system enforces a strict separation between public and private surfaces, ensuring only verified facts appear externally.
